entries.title: Describe a Corpus
entries.description: Creates an empty Corpus and records its provenance, tokenisation, and licence capabilities. Use it before adding Documents to the Corpus.
entries.helpPage:
# Describe a Corpus

`add-corpus` records a Corpus and how it was collected and tokenised. It keeps provenance and licence capabilities so later users can tell what use is permitted.

## When to use it

Use this before adding Documents to a new Corpus. State what the licence permits, including whether the material may be derived from, redistributed, or used commercially; unknown permissions should remain unknown.

## Example

```powershell
motif add-corpus --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --id "stories" --description "Published folktales" --tokeniser "motif-basic" --tokeniser-version "1"
```

## What it prints

Human output confirms the Corpus id and shows its origin, location when supplied, licence, tokenisation, and derivation note.

## Related commands

- [Add a Corpus Document](cmd:add-document) attaches a source to the Corpus.
- [List Corpora](cmd:corpora) finds recorded Corpus ids.
usage: Usage: motif add-corpus --project <fwdata> --id <id> --description <text> --tokeniser <name> --tokeniser-version <v> [--uri <url>] [--licence <text>] [--tokeniser-notes <text>] [--may-derive true|false] [--may-redistribute true|false] [--may-use-commercially true|false] [--requires-attribution true|false] [--licence-basis <text>]

entries.title: Load a Corpus bundle
entries.description: Reads a bundle from a fetching tool and loads each listed source as a Document in its Corpus. The Motif store keeps the fetched text with its provenance and licence details.
entries.helpPage:
# Load a Corpus bundle

`add-corpus-bundle` reads a bundle from a fetching tool, then reads each listed source to add its Document to a Corpus. The bundle records source locations and licences; it does not contain the source text files.

## When to use it

Use this when an outside tool has prepared a Corpus bundle and you want Motif to record its provenance in one step. Inspect the bundle and its licences before loading it.

## Example

```powershell
motif add-corpus-bundle --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --bundle "C:\Temp\stories-bundle.json"
```

## What it prints

Human output identifies the Corpus and document count, then shows its origin, licence, derivation restrictions, and accuracy-claim qualification. Motif stores the fetched text with the Corpus; it does not copy text into the FieldWorks project.

## Related commands

- [Describe a Corpus](cmd:add-corpus) creates the Corpus directly.
- [List Corpora](cmd:corpora) reads Corpora already recorded for the project.
usage: Usage: motif add-corpus-bundle --project <fwdata> --bundle <path>   (the handoff a fetching tool writes)

entries.title: Add a Corpus Document
entries.description: Reads one source file or URL into a named Corpus Document and records its origin and licence details. Use it to preserve where an individual Document came from.
entries.helpPage:
# Add a Corpus Document

`add-document` reads one source file or URL and stores its text as a Document in a named Corpus. It records the source, title, and licence without treating the Document as a FieldWorks Text.

## When to use it

Use this after creating a Corpus when you need to preserve where one article or file came from. Provide a stable Document id and the source location; include licence details for this item when they differ from the Corpus.

## Example

```powershell
motif add-document --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --corpus "stories" --doc "story-12" --source "https://example.org/story-12" --title "The River Path"
```

## What it prints

Human output confirms the Corpus and Document ids and shows the title, source, character count, content hash, and licence when supplied.

## Related commands

- [Describe a Corpus](cmd:add-corpus) records the shared provenance and tokeniser.
- [Show a Corpus](cmd:show-corpus) reads its provenance and licence capabilities.

entries.title: Inspect word analyses
entries.description: Lists manually approved analyses, or adds parser results from a named Assessment when current digests are supplied. It does not run PanGloss.
entries.helpPage:
# Inspect word analyses

`analyses` reads the project's manually approved analyses. With an Assessment id and both current digests, it also returns that Assessment's parser results and says whether they still describe the project.

## When to use it

Use this command when you need to inspect analysis evidence without starting PanGloss. The Assessment form reports whether the current Selection and grammar digests match the evidence.

## Example

```powershell
motif analyses --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## What it prints

Without `--assessment`, the response lists manually approved analyses from a private copy of the saved FieldWorks project. With an Assessment and current Selection and grammar SHA-256 values, it reads manual facts from that Assessment's exact Baseline and includes the stored parser results. Later FieldWorks saves do not change those captured facts. If that Baseline is unavailable, the request is refused.

`projectContext` records whether the manual facts come from the saved project or a Baseline, with the represented source-save time and the exact Baseline token when applicable. The supplied digests describe whether the Assessment still matches the current Selection and grammar; they do not select a different source for its manual facts. JSON returns the same information in a structured response.

## Related commands

- [Read one word's context](cmd:word-context) includes Unknown and Disapproved analyses without an Assessment.
- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) records parser evidence.
- [Query parse statistics](cmd:stats) reads detailed statistics for an Assessment.

entries.title: Apply pending changes
entries.description: Applies the current pending changes to the FieldWorks project as one unit of work. A current Dry Run can waive Correctness for a judgment-only Proposal; mixed changes still need normal Readiness evidence.
entries.helpPage:
# Apply pending changes

`motif apply --all-pending` applies all changes in the current pending Draft Proposal to the FieldWorks project in one unit of work. Motif records a Receipt when it writes changes.

## When to use it

Use this command after reviewing the pending Proposal and while FieldWorks has released the project. FieldWorks should reload the project after Motif reports a write.

A Proposal made only of the bounded Notebook judgment writes can be ready without a Correctness Assessment when its current bound Dry Run shows only Notebook record, owned-text and reserved-field effects. Mixed Proposals still need normal Readiness evidence. The Apply result records whether Correctness was exempt and why; Dry Run, Preflight and Apply still apply.

When Apply is refused with `apply.not-ready`, the current evidence does not satisfy Readiness. A timing-only Trial supplies no Correctness Assessment. A Correctness result with zero approved expectations supplies no comparison of approved readings. In a project with no stems, inspect the recorded parse results and comparisons. `--force` does not skip Readiness here; only [`motif apply <proposalId> --force`](cmd:apply) does, and Autonomous mode refuses `--force` everywhere. A Trial names any grammar the parser dropped with only a warning, such as an environment it could not read. When that dropped grammar is in what the Proposal adds or edits, the Trial is not clean, and Apply is refused with `apply.dropped-grammar` until it is fixed, in the Proposal or in FieldWorks, and the Proposal is tried again. When the parser could not check for dropped grammar, or the Trial was made before the check existed, the Trial says so and is not clean; Apply is then refused with `apply.not-ready` until the Proposal is tried again.

## Example

```text
motif apply --all-pending --project <project> [--revision <r>] [--autonomous] [--message <text>] [--note] [--json]
```

## Mode, message and note

Every Receipt records how the Proposal was applied, `person` or `autonomous`, and a message. With no marker the mode is `person`, and the message defaults to the Proposal's label; `--message <text>` replaces it (one line, at most 128 characters). An agent declares Autonomous mode with `--autonomous` or by setting `MOTIF_AUTONOMOUS=1` in its environment, and an autonomous Apply is refused with `apply.message-required` unless it gives a `--message`; combining Autonomous mode with `--force` is refused with `apply.autonomous-force`. The window always records `person`.

`--note` also writes one Notebook record of the "Motif change" type in the same unit of work as the changes: its title is the Proposal's label, and its text is the Rationale, the Receipt reference and the message. It is off by default. A later Proposal applied with `--note` writes its own note, and the earlier note remains.

## What it prints

The JSON response has `ok`, `applied`, `summary` and, when changes were applied, a `receipt` that carries the Readiness decision. Reload after `applied: true`. When the response carries `apply.reconciliation-needed`, a write may have happened or an earlier one was never confirmed. Reload, open Motif to check the project, and do not retry automatically. A no-op does not need a reload, and an uncertain change stays pending for review.

## Related commands

- [Read the project Overview](cmd:overview) reads stored evidence after you reload the project.

entries.title: Measure a Selection
entries.description: Runs PanGloss over chosen Texts or word forms and stores the resulting Assessments. After FieldWorks saves project changes, capture a new Baseline before measuring them.
entries.helpPage:
# Measure a Selection

`assess` sends a Selection of words through PanGloss and stores the resulting Assessments. It uses the project's stored Baseline when one exists and captures one only when the project has none.

## When to use it

Use this to measure how a grammar parses the project's usual words, named Texts, every wordform, or a supplied word list. After FieldWorks saves grammar changes, capture a new Baseline before measuring them.

To parse some words again and update their main results, pass `--replaces <assessment-id>` with the id of the complete ParseTime Assessment they belong to. The replacement must use that same Baseline and contain only words in that Assessment. Each replaced word keeps the new run's id and measurement time; untouched words keep theirs. A run without `--replaces` records a separate measurement without replacing words in an existing run.

To select words whose recorded parser work exceeds a threshold, use `--retry-work-over <parser-work> --retry-source-assessment <id>`. Words without a recorded work count cannot match this selector.

## Example

```powershell
motif assess "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --all-wordforms --json
```

For an explicit reparse, save the chosen words in a file and name their original run:

```powershell
motif assess "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --words words.txt --replaces <assessment-id> --json
```

## What it prints

Human output reports the Selection and stored Assessment ids, followed by each word's comparison headline and any qualification on a second line. For example, when a completed search builds a Disapproved analysis but misses the word's undecided analysis, it prints “Rebuilt an analysis you Disapproved” and “Your undecided analysis wasn't built”.

Both human output and JSON begin with `counts`: how many words were measured, how many came out `analysed`, `noAnalysis`, `capped` (stopped at the work limit), `timedOut` (stopped at the time safety net) or `skipped`, and among the analysed words how many are `accepted` (some reading identifies every morph in the lexicon) and how many are `guessOnly` (every reading contains a morph the parser had to guess because it could not identify it, such as `a+?baga`). An analysed word is not necessarily an accepted one.

JSON returns the Baseline, Selection, and Assessment results. Each word's `comparison` carries its standing, outcome, stable `meaningCode`, headline, detail, completion flag and tone, plus matched analysis identities and their individual opinions, missing Approved analyses, rebuilt Disapproved analyses and extra readings. This is the same comparison used by the window; display wording is not a grouping identity.

The comparison's `availability` distinguishes `Available` (analysis identities were compared), `RecordedGradesOnly` (recorded reading grades are known, but matched analysis identities are unknown), and `Unavailable` (no morphology comparison was recorded or reconstructed). Unavailable evidence is not a known empty set. An incomplete search makes no claim that an Approved or undecided analysis was not built. No grammar verdict is inferred from the measurements.

## Limits

Assess and Trial use the Default Selection's per-word parser work limit and time policy, including for a supplied word list. A Trial's automatic before Assessment uses the exact limits frozen for the Trial. A stop at the work limit is the same on every computer. A stop at the time safety net varies with machine load, so compare `capped` and `timedOut` separately, and inspect the recorded limits before comparing independent runs. In JSON each stopped word's `stoppedBy` is `work-limit`, `time-safety-net`, or `both` when the work limit and the time safety net both fired inside that word's search; it is read from the word's outcome and the parser's evidence together, so a word that returned readings before a limit fired still names it. A word that was not stopped has no `stoppedBy`. A stopped word is not evidence that no analysis exists.

When object statistics are available, Motif keeps whole-run timing totals and per-object detail for the 2,000 words with the most parser work by default. If parser work are unavailable, it uses time on this computer. A named scope can set `timing-detail-words` in `<project>.motif.toml` to a number from 0 to 10,000. Results identify when word-level detail is incomplete. To keep detail for every word in an explicitly supplied Selection of at most 2,000 words, pass `--full-object-timing` with the Selection. A retry records object timings from the initial pass; it does not supply object timings for the retried result.

Each Assessment has a whole-run time limit, including retries; it is a time on this computer, not a measure of parser work. The project Parsing setting defaults to 3,600 seconds; `--max-seconds <seconds>` overrides it for this run, with a minimum of 60 seconds. If the limit is reached, Motif stops the parser, reports the number of words done and not done, records a `stopped-by-budget` job, and saves no Assessment. The command exits with code 5.

## A large list

`--words <file>` reads a UTF-8 file with one word per line, so a list of thousands of words needs no other preparation. The full JSON result grows with the list. Add `--summary` to print only the counts and one page of words, each with its outcome, whether its reading was accepted or guess-only, its `parserWork` when the parser counted them (a skipped word has none) and its `stoppedBy` when a limit stopped it; `--offset <n>` and `--limit <n>` choose the page (default 25 words from the start), and the output says which words it shows, such as “showing 1-25 of 7206”. The Assessment is stored whole either way.

An agent reads the same summary through the `motif_assess` tool. It returns the counts, one page of words and the stored Assessment id, and pages through that Assessment with `assessment`, `offset` and `limit` rather than measuring again. `wordsFile` names the word file as `--words` does, and giving both `words` and `wordsFile` is refused with `assess.words-ambiguous`. A file that is missing or unreadable is refused with `assess.words-file-unreadable`, and one with no words with `assess.words-file-empty`.

Word files must be at most 8 MiB of valid UTF-8 text without NUL bytes; an initial UTF-8 signature is accepted. A larger file is refused with `assess.words-file-too-large`; invalid UTF-8 or NUL bytes with `assess.words-file-not-text`. Split a large list into smaller files, or save a non-text file as UTF-8 with one word per line, then repeat the call.

## Related commands

- [Show the Default Selection](cmd:selection%20show) reads the usual word list.
- [Read the project Overview](cmd:overview) displays evidence already stored.

entries.title: Capture a Baseline
entries.description: Reads the saved .fwdata project to create or reuse a file-backed Baseline. Use it when the latest FieldWorks save should be the point of comparison for later work.
entries.helpPage:
# Capture a Baseline

`baseline capture --project` reads a saved `.fwdata` file and creates or reuses a file-backed Baseline. You can name a Known project by its name or pass its `.fwdata` path. The capture represents the project as of FieldWorks' last save.

## When to use it

Use this when a later Dry Run or Assessment should be measured against the latest saved project state. FieldWorks may remain open, but unsaved in-memory edits are not part of the capture.

## Example

```powershell
motif baseline capture --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## What it prints

The response identifies the project, Baseline digest, capture time, source save time, and whether the published bytes were reused. JSON returns the Baseline token and capture facts.

## Related commands

- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) ensures a Baseline exists before recording parser evidence.
- [Queue a Baseline Refresh](cmd:baseline-refresh) requests a durable queued capture.

entries.title: Queue a Baseline Refresh
entries.description: Queues a job to capture the project's saved state as a Baseline. Use it when you want to monitor the capture through the job queue.
entries.helpPage:
# Queue a Baseline Refresh

`baseline-refresh` queues durable work to capture the project's saved state as a new Baseline. The job continues after this command exits.

## When to use it

Use this when you want the Baseline capture to run through the job queue and inspect its status later. For an immediate capture, use `baseline capture` instead.

## Example

```powershell
motif baseline-refresh --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata"
```

## What it prints

The command prints the job id when work is queued. Use that id to check whether the Baseline capture completed.

## Related commands

- [Inspect a job](cmd:jobs%20show) reads its current state.
- [Capture a Baseline](cmd:baseline%20capture) performs the synchronous capture.

entries.title: Compare two Assessments
entries.description: Joins two stored Assessments on their shared words and stores the Difference as a new Assessment. It lets you inspect changes without treating the result as a verdict.
entries.helpPage:
# Compare two Assessments

`compare` joins the words shared by two stored Assessments and stores the measured Difference as a new Assessment. It describes measured differences without deciding which run is better.

## When to use it

Use this after two runs when you want to inspect changed results on words present in both Assessments. Choose Assessments from the same Assessor and kind so the measured values have the same meaning; only shared words are compared.

## Example

```powershell
motif compare --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --from <assessmentId> --to <assessmentId> --json
```

## What it prints

Human output shows the new Difference Assessment id and its summary. JSON includes that id, both source Assessment ids, word counts, the Assessor, any tokeniser warning, and the rendered summary text. The command reads stored evidence rather than rerunning either Assessment.

## Related commands

- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) records another Assessment.
- [Read an Assessment report](cmd:report) asks a focused question of one Assessment.

entries.title: Show project settings
entries.description: Reads the project's Assessment scopes and settings. Use it to see the limits and options Motif will use for a later Assessment.
entries.helpPage:
# Show project settings

`config show` reads the named Assessment scopes and related settings stored beside one FieldWorks project.

## When to use it

Use it before measuring when you want to confirm which Assessor, Assessment kinds, or resource limits a named scope selects. A scope provides context for an Assessment; it does not gate whether two measurements can be compared. The Default Selection's parsing limits are saved separately; use [selection show](cmd:selection%20show) to read them.

## Example

```powershell
motif config show --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata"
```

## What it prints

The command prints the saved project settings, or their structured form when `--json` is supplied. It reads configuration and does not run PanGloss.

Each Assessment scope's `timing-detail-words` limits the number of costliest words whose individual object timings are stored. The default is 2,000 and the allowed range is 0–10,000. Set it in `<project>.motif.toml` beside the project, for example:

```toml
[[scope]]
name = "default"
timing-detail-words = 1000
```

Motif keeps the newest 20 standalone Assessments per kind, as well as Assessments needed by current or cited evidence. To change the count, add this project setting:

```toml
[retention]
standalone-assessments-per-kind = 20
```

## Related commands

- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) uses the configured scope when one is named.
- [Show the Default Selection](cmd:selection%20show) reads the project's usual word list.
- [Set Selection limits](cmd:selection%20set-limits) changes its parser work limit or time policy.

entries.title: List Corpora
entries.description: Lists the Corpora and their recorded provenance. Use it to find a Corpus id before adding or inspecting a Document.
entries.helpPage:
# List Corpora

`corpora` lists the Corpora recorded for a FieldWorks project with their provenance summaries.

## When to use it

Use this to find a Corpus id before inspecting it or adding a Document. A Corpus is material Motif holds with provenance; it is not a Text inside the FieldWorks project.

## Example

```powershell
motif corpora --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## What it prints

Human output lists the recorded Corpora. JSON returns their ids and descriptive details for scripts that need to select one.

## Related commands

- [Describe a Corpus](cmd:add-corpus) records a new Corpus.
- [Show a Corpus](cmd:show-corpus) reads one Corpus in detail.

entries.title: Check a grammar
entries.description: Runs the grammar checker against the project's current Baseline and stores its findings. Use warnings to read those findings afterward. The stored-analysis comparison follows the Default proposal checks setting unless the command overrides it.
entries.helpPage:
# Check a grammar

`grammar check` runs the grammar checker against the project's current Baseline and stores its findings. If the project has no Baseline, the command refuses the request; run `motif baseline capture --project <fwdata>` and try again.

## When to use it

Use this to collect diagnostics about the grammar, then read them with `warnings`. It is separate from an Assessment, which measures parsing over a Selection.

## Example

```powershell
motif grammar check --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## How much of the comparison runs

One part of the check re-parses each word to see whether its stored analyses still parse, so it is the part that slows down as a project grows. `--stored-analyses` chooses how much of it runs, for this check only:

- `budget` compares words in order until a fixed amount of work is spent, then reports how many words were left. This is the default.
- `all` compares every word. A large project can take half a minute or more.
- `off` skips the comparison; the checks that need no parsing still run.

Without the flag, the check follows the **Compare stored analyses** choice under *Default proposal checks* in Settings. The same choice applies to the grammar check a Trial runs for a Proposal, so a Proposal's check and the project's are comparable only when they used the same choice.

## What it prints

The response includes the Baseline's lexical entry and rule counts when that inventory is available. Motif advisories are separate from PanGloss findings, so an empty-lexicon note does not change parser severity or Assessment readiness. Error-level findings appear separately from warnings and information. PanGloss can exit nonzero after writing a report with errors; Motif still reads and stores that report. A nonzero exit without a report is a refusal.

Motif also warns when a required inflectional slot in a template has no affixes. The finding names the template, part of speech and slot, and includes the slot's canonical ID. The slot is marked required, but FieldWorks and PanGloss currently treat an empty required slot as optional. Add affixes to express the intended requirement, or mark the slot optional when empty is allowed.

Motif also warns, with code `grammar.negated-feature-value`, about each stored negated feature value (a feature set to "not" a value). FieldWorks' parser loader throws when it reads one, so FieldWorks cannot parse with the project, while PanGloss parses on and leaves the value out of the stem's features, so what carries it is not held back by it. The finding names the feature, the value and the entry or object that holds it. On a stem or an inflectional affix, [remove the feature value](cmd:compose-remove-feature-value) (it removes a negated one like a closed one), then author a closed value if one is wanted. Motif has no command for a negated value in a phoneme, natural class or part of speech, and whether FieldWorks can clear one was not checked.

Motif also warns, with code `grammar.derived-stem-keeps-from-class`, about each derivational affix that takes a From Inflection Class and names no To Inflection Class: the stems it derives keep the From class, so an inflectional affix that attaches only to other classes finds no stem. The finding names the affix and the class. Set the class the derived stem should take with [Restrict a derivational affix](cmd:compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction) (`toInflectionClass`), or leave it when the derived stem does keep its class.

Motif also warns, with code `grammar.template-has-no-slots`, about each affix template that has no slot. LibLCM can hold one, so Motif authors it without refusing, but it holds no affix position and adds nothing the parser can use. The finding names the template and its part of speech. Add a slot with [Add an affix slot](cmd:compose-author-affix-slot) and put the template's affixes in it; a slot that may be empty is an optional slot.

Motif also warns, with code `grammar.phoneme-case-alias-missing`, when a featured lowercase phoneme lacks an explicit titlecase or uppercase representation on that same phoneme. It checks the default vernacular writing system's casing, including its case alias, in every phoneme set. The finding names the missing spellings: `c` needs `C`, and `ng` needs both `Ng` and `NG`. Implicit writing-system letters have no phonological features and can unify with unrelated featured sounds. Add the missing spellings with [Edit a phoneme](cmd:compose-edit-phoneme); review an existing capital phoneme's identity and class membership before merging it. Accented sounds remain distinct. This is advice and does not prevent authoring.

Motif also warns, with code `grammar.phoneme-spelling-ambiguous`, about each phoneme whose spelling is the spellings of two or more other phonemes joined, as `ng` beside `n` and `g`. The parser reads letters as the longest spelling at each point and keeps one reading, so `ng` is always the one phoneme and a word where `n` and `g` meet across a morpheme boundary is never read as those two. A digraph whose parts are not phonemes (`sh` with no `s` or `h`) is not flagged. The finding names the phoneme and the spellings it is made of. Write the affected form of the affix or stem as an allomorph spelled with the digraph, or change the orthography to remove the ambiguity (Black, section 6.3.3). Do not remove the phoneme: every rule that uses it would break. Every phoneme set is checked. The spelling may be intended, as `aa` beside `a`, and then nothing needs changing.

Motif also warns, with code `grammar.allomorph-environment-ignored-by-parser`, about each stem or affix form that names an environment the parser cannot read, as one written with a morpheme boundary `+`. The parser drops such an environment, so the form is not restricted by it and may appear anywhere. The check uses the same recognizer as FieldWorks' parser loader over the project's phonemes and natural classes. PanGloss drops the environment too, but its own grammar-health report does not list it. Entries marked do-not-use-for-parsing are skipped. The finding names the form and the environment. Rewrite the environment with phonemes and natural classes only. A restriction that needs a morpheme boundary can be stated as a phonological rule with a boundary context ([Author a phonological rule](cmd:compose-author-phonological-rule)); Motif has not checked that this gives the same readings as the environment, so try it in a Trial.

Motif also warns, with code `grammar.allomorph-repeats-environment-material`, about each stem or affix form that already ends with the literal material to the right of the slot in every environment it names (or starts with the material to its left), as `batan-ung` before the linker `ng`, where the form meant to stop before the linker was `batan-u`. It refuses nothing: an affix such as Tagalog `pang` before `ng` is correct, because the environment restricts the neighbour. Natural classes, boundaries and optional parts are ignored. The finding names the form and the environment.

Motif also reports lexicon hygiene as warnings, with three codes. It only reports; it changes nothing, and it includes entries marked do-not-parse, which FieldWorks still parses. `lexicon.stem-typed-as-content-word` names each stem whose part of speech is a Noun, Verb or Adjective (or a sub-category of one) and whose form is a single letter or whose gloss begins with `=`, `see:`, `see also` or `see under` (a cross-reference stub), begins with `letter`, or names a function word (`marker`, `particle`, `interjection`, `conjunction`, `preposition`, `determiner`, `linker`, `pause word`). Such a stem takes that category's inflection and derivation, so it lets short unrelated readings parse. `lexicon.duplicate-entry` names entries that share a lexeme form, a first gloss, a morph type and a category. `lexicon.affix-hyphen-on-wrong-side` names a prefix, proclitic or prefixing-interfix form written `-i` and a suffix, enclitic or suffixing-interfix form written `i-`; the hyphen belongs on the side that touches the stem. When there are more than 20 findings of one kind, one finding gives the total and a sample of five. To fix the first kind in bulk, put `compose-set-stem-part-of-speech` intents in one [`compose-batch`](cmd:compose-batch) file.

## Related commands

- [Read grammar warnings](cmd:warnings) filters and displays stored findings.
- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) measures parser behavior rather than grammar diagnostics.

entries.title: Prepare an AI Handoff
entries.description: Writes a folder with the grammar and selected Texts, plus retained parse evidence when an invocation is selected. The files contain real project data, so review them before sharing.
entries.helpPage:
# Prepare an AI Handoff

`handoff` writes a folder containing a grammar and selected Texts, plus retained parse evidence when an invocation is selected. The folder includes a short orientation and a Python helper; the full format and parser references are linked online and require network access.

## When to use it

Use a retained invocation when you want its Baseline, Selection, and parse evidence in the Handoff. Use `--no-assess` for a Baseline-only Handoff; `--texts` can then restrict which Texts are included. The folder contains real language data, so inspect it before sharing it with a chat model.

The command line needs one of `--invocation` or `--no-assess`; without either it prints its usage and does not run. `--texts` is accepted only with `--no-assess`. The AI Handoff controls in Settings use the same command but parses the chosen words fresh before writing, and Motif refuses another parse request for the project until that Handoff finishes.

## Example

```powershell
motif handoff "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --out "C:\Temp\koro-handoff" --invocation <invocationId> --json
```

## What it prints

Human output reports the output directory, the Baseline's source save time, Selection size, file count, and Assessment ids. With `--no-assess`, the Baseline-only Handoff has four files and no Assessment ids. JSON includes the output directory, Baseline and Selection, relative file paths in alphabetical order, invocation and Assessment ids, and the Handoff text fields. An assessed folder lists `grammar.json`, `handoff.md`, `parse-results.json`, `read_results.py`, then `texts.json`; a Baseline-only folder omits `parse-results.json`. The window's **AI Handoff for this word** action keeps the diagnostic already shown in Why This Analysis? and the Baseline recorded with it; it does not run a new Assessment or trace, includes `traces/<word>.trace.json`, and omits `parse-results.json`. Motif builds the folder beside the destination and moves it into place only after it is complete.

entries.helpPage:
# Inspect a job

`jobs show` reads the stored status of one durable job for a project.

## When to use it

Use this after a command returns a job id, or when a job appears in the queue. A job can represent a Baseline Refresh, Dry Run, Trial, or Parsimony measurement; its status shows where that work is in its lifecycle.

## Example

```powershell
motif jobs show <jobId> --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## What it prints

Human output shows the job kind, status, attempt number, update time, queue order, and the stage a Parsimony job is in when available. JSON returns the structured status, cancellation and failure details, queue order, Trial word progress, and the Parsimony stage (`stageProgress`) when available.

## A job whose runner stopped

A job a runner claimed keeps a lease that the runner renews. If the lease runs out, the runner stopped and nothing is working on the job. JSON then adds `"claimLost": true` and a `warnings` entry with the code `job.claim-lost`; human output prints the same note. When the job was parked waiting for something that now exists, the status shown is `queued`, the status the next runner gives it, and the warning names the stored status. A job a runner parked on purpose, such as `waiting-for-project-host`, is not claimed, so it shows its stored status and no warning. `claimLost` and `warnings` are left out when the claim is fine.

The CLI starts a runner from `jobs show` when the job is queued or its claim was lost, so the job moves without another command. The MCP `motif_job` tool only reports; it does not start a runner.

- [List queued jobs](cmd:jobs%20list) finds jobs across Known projects.

entries.helpPage:
# Choose a Default Selection

`selection set-default` saves which project Texts and added words Motif measures when a command does not name another Selection. It also saves the Selection's parser work limit and estimated or explicit time policy.

## When to use it

Use this to focus repeatable Assessments on a linguist-chosen set of material. Texts are identified by GUID, not by title, and added words can be included even when they do not occur in a Text.

## Example

```powershell
motif selection set-default --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --name "Verb examples" --texts <textGuid> --add-words "mala,ma" --parser-work-limit 20000000 --time-mode estimated
```

Use `--time-mode explicit --time-limit-ms <positive>` for a chosen time safety net, in milliseconds on this computer. `--time-mode estimated` rejects `--time-limit-ms`; `--parser-work-limit none` stores no step or time cap. To replace an existing Selection, first read its revision with [selection show](cmd:selection%20show) and pass it as `--expected-revision`.

## A word list with counts

`--words-file <path>` takes the added words from a UTF-8 file, in place of `--add-words`. Each line is a word, or a word, a tab and a whole-number count. There is no header line, and the file is at most 8 MiB.

- A plain list of words gives no counts. A word with no count has a count that is not known, which is not the same as zero.
- Words are stored in NFD. A word on several lines has its counts added up.
- Motif stores the file's name and its SHA-256 with the Selection, so you can tell which list the counts came from.
- A later save that names no file keeps the stored list when the Texts and added words are the same, and any other change to the Texts or words drops it.
- A Selection of chosen Texts ranks its words by places in those Texts. A Selection with no Texts ranks them by the file's counts, and the Overview then names its bands By Frequency Band, never Text Coverage.
- The window shows the same count beside each word in the word list of a Selection with no Texts, most often used first. A word the file gave no count has a blank there, and a count of zero shows as zero. Once the words are edited so they are no longer the saved list, the counts are blank until the Selection is saved with a list.

```powershell
motif selection set-default --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --name "Frequent words" --words-file .\frequencies.tsv
```

## What it prints

The command reports the saved Selection name and its settings. Add `--json` to receive the structured Selection response.

## Related commands

- [List project Texts](cmd:texts%20list) finds Text GUIDs to select.

entries.title: Inspect parse timing
entries.description: Reads timing evidence for an Assessment, optionally narrowed to words or grouped by kind or rule. Use it to locate expensive parsing work after an Assessment.
entries.helpPage:
# Inspect parse timing

`timing` reads timing measurements recorded in an Assessment. It can narrow the result to words and group costs by kind or rule. Add `--proposal <id>` to use the latest Trial's measurements.

## When to use it

Use this when an Assessment shows costly parsing and you want to identify which rules or kinds account for the parser's work. Name an Assessment when the project has more than one measurement.

Without `--assessment`, Timing reads the Default Selection's current results, including explicit replacements made with `assess --replaces`. Naming an Assessment reads its original words and measurements. Explicit timing overrides replace only words that run measured; they cannot add other words to it.

## Example

```powershell
motif timing --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --proposal <proposalId> --by rule --top 10
```

## What it prints

The command compares parser work only when the Trial retained a compatible Baseline Assessment for the selected words. It reports the percentage change for the selected scope and individual words. Object changes require complete work counters for the same words and a matching object identity on both sides. A new object, missing detail, a stopped search, a zero Baseline or an incompatible parser makes the affected comparison unavailable; the command gives a reason instead of estimating it.

`--rule` takes `kind:key`, such as `morph_rule:12345678-1234-1234-abcd-123456789abc`. Names are display labels; object identities distinguish rules with the same name. `--json` returns the comparisons as structured data.

JSON identifies each word's producing Assessment, invocation and measurement time. It also records the selected run's Baseline and captured FieldWorks save, when available. Its evidence relationship distinguishes Current, Historical, SavedSince and Unknown; current-project freshness is reported separately, so a new Baseline does not make an old measurement current.

## Related commands

- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) creates timing evidence.
- [Query parse statistics](cmd:stats) forwards a query to PanGloss for detailed counts.

entries.title: Trace a word
entries.description: Runs PanGloss for one word against the project's current Baseline and returns its diagnostic. Use it to inspect recorded analyses and trace events.
entries.helpPage:
# Trace a word

`trace` runs PanGloss for one word against the project's current Baseline and reads the diagnostic shown by Why This Analysis?. Add `--proposal <id>` to trace against that Proposal's Trial copy. It does not change the project or store a new Assessment.

## Trace a word now

```powershell
motif trace --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --word mirusi
```

Add `--json` to get the typed response, including the shared `reading` and the diagnostic's recorded provenance. A clean process exit does not establish that the parser's work limit or time safety net was not reached; when the diagnostic cannot report that, completion is unknown.

If the project has no Baseline, capture one with `motif baseline capture --project <fwdata>` before tracing. Trace uses that saved grammar; it does not inspect unsaved FieldWorks changes.

For an unparsed word, text output names the shape whose recorded lexical lookup found no root and explains recorded refusal codes. A stem that reaches an unapplied required template has a different reason from an attempt that builds the wrong surface. A recorded code can be explained without an owner's detailed explanation; absent details remain unavailable. A trace without recorded reasons says so, and an unfinished search cannot establish that the word has no analysis.

When Motif captures a trace, `hostCapture.lexiconEntryCount` records the number of lexical entries in the exact Baseline or Trial copy used. A completed trace with an empty lexicon names that fact and the word, instead of guessing which affix or spelling is wrong. A missing count is unknown. Saved traces retain this count and their recorded reasons without opening the current project.

## Trace a Trial report case

A report-bound trace selects an exact case and side: `motif proposal trial --project <fwdata> <proposalId> --report <reportId> --case <caseKey> --trace --side after`. Motif uses the recorded parser, grammar and limits or explains that the exact inputs are unavailable. The diagnostic has its own identity and completion; it does not alter the batch report.

## Read a saved trace

```powershell
motif trace --load "C:\Temp\mirusi.trace.json"
```

`--load` reads the saved PanGloss diagnostic without opening a project or running a parser. It uses the same reader as a live trace, so the returned word, analyses, attempts, and recorded tree share one interpretation. Why This Analysis? translates the recorded refusal code into a sentence while retaining the code and the original evidence. A rule or required feature is named only when recorded; neighboring events do not establish which rule caused a failure. The window folds forward building events into Plain and keeps the full parser order in Expert.

## Related commands

- [Load a saved trace](cmd:trace%20--load) reads a diagnostic without a parser.
- [Prepare an AI Handoff](cmd:handoff) writes project context and retained parse evidence.
- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) records parse results for chosen words.

entries.title: Read grammar warnings
entries.description: Reads stored grammar findings and allomorph refusals from parsing, with filters by code or warning level. Confirmed uses of Selection words stay separate from spelling and membership matches.
entries.helpPage:
# Read grammar warnings

`warnings` reads grammar-check findings and allomorph refusals already recorded by parsing for a project. It can filter by diagnostic code or show only findings at warning level. Add `--proposal <id>` to read the check stored with that Proposal's latest Trial. When the current Baseline has not been checked, `warnings` refuses and tells you to run `grammar check`; it does not return an empty findings list.

PanGloss reports an unreadable phonological environment as a warning. Roots ignore that restriction but keep valid ones; ordinary affixes add an unrestricted pass beside valid passes; an infix with no valid position is skipped.

## When to use it

Use it after [Check a grammar](cmd:grammar%20check) when you want to inspect reported findings. Combine `--kind` and `--left-out` to narrow a large result without rerunning the check.

## Example

```powershell
motif warnings --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --left-out --json
```

## What it prints

The response includes separate error, warning, and information counts, plus findings with PanGloss-owned titles, explanations, guidance, optional background, verified FieldWorks places, subjects, and links where available. Information can identify a stored analysis that PanGloss no longer reproduces, name the rule that changed its surface, or explain why the loss could not be attributed. Each finding retains the report locale. Missing references and project settings have explicit statuses and unavailable-link reasons. `--left-out` keeps warning-level findings only. Without a Baseline, the command refuses and tells you to run `motif baseline capture --project <fwdata>`. When a Baseline has no stored check, it refuses and tells you to run `motif grammar check --project <fwdata>`.

The response includes the Baseline's lexical entry and rule counts when that inventory is available. Motif advisories are listed separately from parser findings.

Motif findings include `grammar.required-slot-empty` when a required inflectional slot in a template has no affixes. Each finding names the template, part of speech, slot and canonical slot ID. The slot is marked required, but FieldWorks and PanGloss currently treat an empty required slot as optional.

Motif findings also include `grammar.negated-feature-value` for a stored negated feature value, which FieldWorks' parser loader cannot read. Each finding names the feature, the value and the object that holds it, and, for a stem or inflectional affix, points to [removing the feature value](cmd:compose-remove-feature-value); for other objects it says Motif has no command for it.

Motif findings also include `grammar.derived-stem-keeps-from-class` for a derivational affix with a From Inflection Class and no To Inflection Class. Each finding names the affix and the class its derived stems keep, and says to set a To Inflection Class when they belong to another class.

Motif findings also include `grammar.template-has-no-slots` for an affix template with no slot, which the parser cannot use. Each finding names the template and its part of speech and says to add a slot.

Motif findings also include `grammar.phoneme-case-alias-missing` when a featured lowercase phoneme lacks titlecase or uppercase spellings on the same phoneme. It names the missing aliases and points to [Edit a phoneme](cmd:compose-edit-phoneme), so implicit featureless capitals do not admit unintended analyses.

Motif findings also include `grammar.phoneme-spelling-ambiguous` for a phoneme whose spelling is other phonemes' spellings joined (`ng` beside `n` and `g`), which the parser always reads as the longest spelling, and `grammar.allomorph-environment-ignored-by-parser` for a form whose environment the parser cannot read and so drops, leaving the form unrestricted by it. Each finding names the phoneme or form and says what to change.

Motif findings also include `grammar.allomorph-repeats-environment-material` for a form that already spells the material its environment asks of its neighbour (`batan-ung` before `ng`); it is a second look, not a refusal.

Motif findings also include three lexicon hygiene warnings: `lexicon.stem-typed-as-content-word` for a Noun, Verb or Adjective stem that is a single letter, a cross-reference stub or a function word by its gloss, `lexicon.duplicate-entry` for entries with the same form and first gloss, and `lexicon.affix-hyphen-on-wrong-side` for a prefix written `-i` or a suffix written `i-`. They report only; see [`grammar-check`](cmd:grammar%20check) for what each looks for and how to fix many at once.

When a stored Assessment matches the Baseline and Selection, all recorded allomorph segmentation refusals are included under `parse.allomorph.unsegmentable`, labelled **Parse all words**. Their descriptions preserve the parser's reason, without truncating the allomorph list or inventing guidance. These findings can differ from the whole-grammar check's findings.

## Your words

When a stored Assessment from [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) matches the current Baseline and Selection, each finding lists the words in the Selection reached by its subjects, with their meanings, such as Lost or Kept. The headline counts exact uses only, once per word, and says how many of those don't parse. Membership and spelling candidates have separate counts and never enter that headline. Each kind of finding gets the same separate counts.

Motif finds the words from the object the finding names, by its FieldWorks identity:

- an allomorph or grammatical info: the FieldWorks or parser analyses that use it;
- an entry or an environment: the FieldWorks or parser analyses that use its allomorphs;
- a sense: the FieldWorks or parser analyses that use its grammatical info;
- a natural class: the allomorphs its environments condition, and the words the phonological rules that name it ran in;
- a rule: the words its stored per-word timings say it ran in.
- a feature definition, value or specification: the allomorphs, grammatical infos and rules whose feature specifications name it;
- a stem name or inflection class: the allomorphs or grammatical infos that refer to it;
- a boundary: the allomorphs and rules whose contexts name it.

Templates and slots reach words using their affixes as **membership candidates**. Inflection types, ad hoc prohibitions, phoneme sets and feature systems also reach members as candidates: using a member does not prove a parse selected the named resource.

Letters and phonemes reach **spelling candidates; not confirmed uses of the phoneme**. Spelling uses case-insensitive, canonically decomposed substring matching, which cannot establish phoneme identity. A feature owned by a phoneme keeps that same limit, including when reached through its feature system. A phoneme set follows its members' grammar references and omits spelling candidates.

For a word with no analysis, an allomorph or entry also reaches spelling candidates through the vernacular forms recorded for the Baseline. This includes typed words the parser refused. The window calls these **spelling matches**, lists the words, and never presents the spelling alone as an exact use.

For each finding, exact uses take precedence over membership candidates, then spelling candidates. The lists never share a word. The overall counts apply that precedence across all findings, too. The words show use, not cause: a word that uses what a warning names may fail for some other reason.

Every finding has an attribution state. A supported route with no matching word says **none in this Selection**. A project resource without word attribution says **project-wide**. A **missing object** distinguishes a GUID absent from the checked Baseline from one belonging to a different FieldWorks class. **Unresolved identity** distinguishes no subject, a named subject without a project GUID, and a class with no supported route.

Features also follow shared references to their enclosing complex specifications. If some feature owners have no supported route or no word attribution, the finding retains those attribution limits alongside any exact uses or candidates. When no owner has a supported route, the finding reports the limit rather than claiming there are no words in the Selection.

Without a matching Assessment, supported routes say **evidence unavailable**; their counts are absent rather than zero. Missing and unresolved subjects retain their specific reasons. Motif refuses stores with an older shape and asks the developer to delete the database so it can recreate it.

## Related commands

- [Check a grammar](cmd:grammar%20check) records fresh findings.
- [Read the project Overview](cmd:overview) includes the warning count with other stored evidence.

entries.helpPage:
# Read one word's context

`word-context` reads one word's captured FieldWorks presence and all of its stored analyses, including Approved, Disapproved and Unknown opinions. It uses the same query as the word panel and does not require an Assessment or membership in a Selection.

## Example

```text
motif word-context --project Koro.fwdata --word dogs --json
```

## What it prints

The response includes the exact Baseline identity, its source-save and publication times, word membership, each stored analysis with its identity and individual opinion, and an exact Word Analyses link when available. `isStale` says whether the saved FieldWorks project is newer than the Baseline's source save. A later save does not replace the captured analyses.

Before a Baseline exists, membership is unknown and no analysis context is supplied; this does not mean the word is absent. A missing Baseline file is refused. When several wordforms have the same form, their stored analyses retain their own identities and no unique navigation target is invented.

## Related commands

- [Capture a Baseline](cmd:baseline%20capture) records the saved project state.
- [Inspect approved analyses](cmd:analyses) reads the approved-analysis aggregate.
- [Trace a word](cmd:trace) records the parser's search.

entries.helpPage:
# Reading a Handoff

Start with `handoff.md` for the included files and reading examples; use the separate `pastedHeader` text for the prepared chat prompt.

An assessed Handoff lists files alphabetically: `grammar.json`, `handoff.md`, `parse-results.json`, `read_results.py`, then `texts.json`. A Baseline-only Handoff omits `parse-results.json`. The App's one-word Handoff contains `grammar.json`, `handoff.md`, `read_results.py`, `texts.json`, then `traces/<word>.trace.json`; it carries the raw diagnostic and omits batch parse results.

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `grammar.json` | The grammar Motif exports for PanGloss to parse. |
| `handoff.md` | Explains the included material and gives reading examples. |
| `parse-results.json` | One result for each selected word, including its parser outcome and timing. |
| `read_results.py` | Queries the Handoff's JSON files from a terminal. |
| `texts.json` | The selected Texts with the analyses the project stores. |
| `traces/<word>.trace.json` | The raw diagnostic for the selected word, including parser fields Motif does not interpret. |

Read the files as linguistic project data; they may contain real grammar rules, lexicon entries, and text.

Use the helper’s own help to see its commands, then ask focused questions against the supplied files:

```powershell
python read_results.py --help
python read_results.py word --help
```

For an assessed folder, the current CLI exports a retained Assessment invocation rather than silently running a fresh one. To create one, first run [assess](cmd:assess) with `--json`, read `invocationId` from its response, then pass that value to [handoff](cmd:handoff):

```powershell
motif handoff "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --out "C:\handoffs\Sena" --invocation <invocationId> --json
```

The successful JSON response reports `outputDirectory`, `baseline`, `selection`, `files`, `assessmentIds`, optional `invocationId`, `pastedHeader`, and `handoffMarkdown`. Use `--no-assess` for a folder without `parse-results.json`; `--texts <guid,guid>` is accepted only with that option, to select texts.

Treat every file as potentially sensitive and share it only with a service approved for that project.

entries.title: Measuring a grammar
entries.description: These commands answer different questions. grammar check asks PanGloss to inspect the whole grammar and stores findings for the current Baseline. It does not parse selected words. assess parses a Selection and records one or more Assessments. overview reads stored summaries; stats queries statistics from a stored run.
entries.helpPage:
# Measuring a grammar

These commands answer different questions. `grammar check` asks PanGloss to inspect the whole grammar and stores findings for the current [Baseline](term:baseline). It does not parse selected words. `assess` parses a Selection and records one or more [Assessments](term:assessment). `overview` reads stored summaries; `stats` queries statistics from a stored run.

Capture a Baseline explicitly with [baseline capture](cmd:baseline%20capture) when you want to name that step:

```powershell
motif baseline capture --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
```

Then use [assess](cmd:assess) to measure the saved Default Selection, or name a source such as all wordforms. Read stored summaries with [overview](cmd:overview) and query statistics by replaying the retained parser evidence and cache for a stored Assessment with [stats](cmd:stats):

```powershell
motif assess "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --all-wordforms --json
motif overview --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
motif stats "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
```

`assess` is synchronous in the current CLI. If you give no Selection flags, it uses the saved Default Selection. Other supported sources include `--texts <guid,guid>`, `--words <file>`, and retry options such as `--retry-failed --retry-source-assessment <id>`. The command ensures a Baseline exists if needed.

The successful `assess --json` response includes the invocation identifier and the Assessment records produced. For example, its relevant fields have this shape:

```json
{
  "invocationId": "<invocation-id>",
  "assessmentIds": ["<assessment-id>"],
  "measurements": [
    {
      "assessmentId": "<assessment-id>",
      "kind": "ObjectTiming",
      "invocationId": "<invocation-id>"
    }
  ]
}
```

Use `invocationId` when you need to create a [Handoff](cmd:handoff) for this exact retained run. The number and kinds of `measurements` can vary with the Assessor’s supported kinds; do not assume a fixed Assessment count.

Use [grammar check](cmd:grammar%20check) to check the whole grammar. [warnings](cmd:warnings) reads findings that have already been stored:

```powershell
motif grammar check --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
motif warnings --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
```

`warnings` reads findings already stored for that Baseline; it does not rerun the check. Without a Baseline, `grammar check` refuses and tells you to run `motif baseline capture --project <fwdata>`. Use **Working with jobs** for commands that enqueue background work.

entries.title: Output and exit codes
entries.description: Use the process exit code as the success signal. Successful text output goes to stdout; handled failures go to stderr. With --json, successful responses are usually the command’s JSON object itself, using camelCase fields, not a common success wrapper. Some enqueue-only commands return a bare job ID even with --json.
entries.helpPage:
# Output and exit codes

Use the process exit code as the success signal. Successful text output goes to stdout; handled failures go to stderr. With `--json`, successful responses are usually the command’s JSON object itself, using camelCase fields, not a common success wrapper. Some enqueue-only commands return a bare job ID even with `--json`.

Handled failures requested with `--json` write a failure object to stderr and nothing to stdout. Its shape is:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "reason": "Busy",
  "message": "<human-readable reason>",
  "detail": { "project": "<project path>" }
}
```

`code` and `detail` are optional. The `reason` is a stable failure class; `message` is for a person. Exit codes are `1` for an invalid invocation, `2` for a refusal, missing item, or cancellation, `3` when the request cannot be attempted now (such as a busy project), `4` for an inconsistent store or unexpected failure, and `5` when an Assessment stops at its whole-run time limit. Retry a `3` later; do not retry a refusal unchanged.

The `help` command has its own plain stderr errors and exits `2` for invalid help syntax or an unknown entry; it does not use the failure object. An unexpected exception escaping the top-level command handler exits `4`; with `--json` it writes the failure object with code `cli.unexpected`, and without it a plain `error: ...` line. A command stopped by Ctrl+C exits `2` with code `cli.cancelled`, as a failure object with `--json` or a plain `cli.cancelled: ...` line without it. Treat any nonzero exit as failure and keep stdout and stderr separate.

entries.title: Using Motif from an agent
entries.description: Call Motif as motif <verb> .... Each process handles one command; durable project state is stored between calls, so commands do not depend on a setup command in the same process. Use an explicit project path with commands that accept --project or take the .fwdata path as a positional argument.
entries.helpPage:
# Using Motif from an agent

Call Motif as `motif <verb> ...`. Each process handles one command; durable project state is stored between calls, so commands do not depend on a setup command in the same process. Use an explicit project path with commands that accept `--project` or take the `.fwdata` path as a positional argument.

Prefer `--json` when the command’s usage line supports it, and read the response from stdout. Do not parse the human text rendering. For example:

```powershell
motif overview --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
motif assess "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --all-wordforms --json
motif jobs list --json
```

To list help entries in one call, run `motif help --all --json`. The JSON has a `locale`, a `siteRoot`, and `entries` for available CLI commands, glossary terms and Guide pages. Each entry has a kind, code, slug, title, description, a `helpPage` field containing the full Help page Markdown when a page exists, and a URL; command entries also include usage lines and a surface. For one entry, `motif help <code>` prints its title, description, URL, and (for a command) usage. Add `--full` to print the expanded page, or `--json` to get that entry's metadata, including its full Help page when available. The documentation website also publishes `llms.txt`, a plain-text index of every page. With no arguments, `motif` prints the usage catalog to stderr and exits with code 1.

Assistants need Advanced AI mode to use MCP tools. In the window, open **AI Assistants**, select **Let Assistants Use Motif's Tools**, then choose which assistants to connect. The **AI Assistants** Guide page explains the client steps. A person can also enable it with `motif settings advanced-ai on`. The MCP server starts with `motif mcp`; each project tool takes a Known project name or recorded path in its `project` argument. Use the workflow resource to draft, Dry Run, Trial, revise and Finalize for a person to review and Apply. Most commands run synchronously, but `baseline-refresh`, `dry-run`, and `trial` enqueue jobs. See **Working with jobs**. For errors and retry decisions, see **Output and exit codes**.

Before composing rules, read the encoding guide for the phenomenon: `motif help` lists the guides, and `motif help guide:encoding/workflow --full` shows the working order. Over MCP the same text is the `motif_guide` tool.

A completed Trial has a saved report. Read its summary and limitations, then use failures or full detail to page through the cases needed for review. In MCP, `motif_trial` reads and refreshes reports explicitly, and `motif_difference` reads a particular report or its cases; a trace is an explicit diagnostic. No red flags means only not bad, never good.

entries.title: Working with jobs
entries.description: The Motif job runner handles durable work that outlives the command that queued it. baseline-refresh, dry-run and trial enqueue jobs. A synchronous assess command is not a job.
entries.helpPage:
# Working with jobs

The Motif job runner handles durable work that outlives the command that queued it. [baseline-refresh](cmd:baseline-refresh), `dry-run` and `trial` enqueue jobs. A synchronous [assess](cmd:assess) command is not a job.

```powershell
motif jobs list --json
motif jobs show <jobId> --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
motif jobs assessments <jobId> --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
motif jobs cancel <jobId> --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
motif jobs requeue <jobId> --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
motif jobs move <jobId> --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --to-top --json
```

[`jobs list`](cmd:jobs%20list) spans every Known project and reports active work in queue order; it is the jobs command that does not take `--project`. [`jobs show`](cmd:jobs%20show) returns the job’s status, attempt, update time, cancellation request, failure category, version, and queue position when available. Status values are lower-case hyphenated strings such as `waiting-for-project-host`. A status response has fields like:

```json
{
  "jobId": "<job-id>",
  "projectKey": "<project-key>",
  "found": true,
  "kind": "trial",
  "status": "waiting-for-project-host",
  "attempt": 1,
  "updatedUtc": "<UTC timestamp>",
  "cancellationRequested": false,
  "failureCategory": null,
  "version": 1,
  "queueOrder": 1
}
```

A job whose claiming runner stopped adds `"claimLost": true` and a `warnings` array to the status response; each warning has a `code` and a `message`, and the code for this case is `job.claim-lost`. If the job was parked waiting for something that now exists, `status` is `queued`, the status the next runner gives it. A job parked on purpose, such as `waiting-for-project-host`, has released its claim, so it shows that status with no warning. `claimLost` and `warnings` are left out otherwise. The CLI starts a runner when `jobs show` or `--wait` sees a queued or claim-lost job; the MCP `motif_job` tool only reports, so run any command that queues work, or start `SIL.Motif.Worker`, to restart a runner.

The queue-list response is `{ "jobs": [...] }`. Each entry includes `jobId`, `projectKey`, `projectPath`, `kind`, `status`, `attempt`, `updatedUtc`, and `queueOrder`. `jobs assessments` returns `jobId` and an `assessments` array whose entries contain `assessmentId`, `assessor`, `kind`, and `savedUtc`.

[`jobs cancel`](cmd:jobs%20cancel) on a queued or parked job moves it to cancelled. Cancelling a running job requests cancellation; the runner completes it. [`jobs requeue`](cmd:jobs%20requeue) is for a terminal job and creates a fresh attempt with a new job ID. Use [`jobs assessments`](cmd:jobs%20assessments) to read the Assessment IDs produced by a completed job.

Without `--wait`, enqueueing `dry-run` or `trial` returns a bare job ID, including under `--json`. With `--wait`, the CLI waits up to two minutes by default; `--wait-timeout-ms <ms>` changes the bound. See **Output and exit codes** for the failure shape and exit mapping.

entries.title: Ask the linguist when evidence runs out
entries.description: Ask when two analyses fit the evidence and choosing between them changes the Proposal. A useful question lets the linguist distinguish those analyses using forms already in the project and one concrete prediction.
entries.helpPage:
# Ask the linguist when evidence runs out

Ask when two analyses fit the evidence and choosing between them changes the Proposal. A useful question lets the linguist distinguish those analyses using forms already in the project and one concrete prediction.

## Guess, ask or defer

- **Guess** only a low-impact, reversible choice that the existing evidence supports; keep it in a Draft and check it with a Dry Run and Trial.
- **Ask** when the linguist can answer a concrete contrast. Ask one question at a time and show the evidence plus the competing predictions.
- **Defer** when the project lacks the forms or the linguist cannot yet distinguish the choices. State what evidence would resolve the choice, and do not invent a Proposal.
- **Say the tool is missing** when Motif cannot create a required FieldWorks object. Explain the needed encoding and wait for a composer; do not imitate it with a different object.

When the project has no evidence for requested forms, do not suggest an affix shape, allomorph or example word, even as a prediction or an unapplied draft. Say what attested forms and contexts would resolve the question, then ask for them.

For example: “I can’t determine this pattern from the project. Could you share attested forms in the relevant contexts, including a contrasting form if available?”

## Build the question from evidence

Read forms with `motif_lexicon`, `motif_word` or `motif_texts`. Use the actual spellings and contexts returned for this project. Do not present guessed forms as attested; when requested forms are absent, ask for attested forms instead of predicting spellings.

Use this frame and replace every bracketed item with project evidence:

> “I found `<attested form A>` in `<observed context A>` and `<attested form B>` in `<observed context B>`. The two analyses predict `<predicted form A>` versus `<predicted form B>` for `<unobserved or contrasting context>`. Which form would a speaker use there?”

Ask for the missing fact only. Do not bundle a request to choose the analysis, name a rule, provide more examples and approve a Proposal into one question.

## Common wrong choices

- Guessing a high-impact choice the evidence does not support.
- Asking several questions at once, or with forms that are not attested in the project.

entries.title: Phonologically conditioned allomorphs
entries.description: A linguist sees one morpheme with different spoken or written forms in different sound contexts. FieldWorks can keep those forms together and condition each one on its surrounding sounds.
entries.helpPage:
# Phonologically conditioned allomorphs

A linguist sees one morpheme with different spoken or written forms in different sound contexts. FieldWorks can keep those forms together and condition each one on its surrounding sounds.

## Encode the pattern

- Keep the variants under one lexical entry when the evidence supports one morpheme.
- Give each variant the sound environment where it occurs. Use a natural class when several sounds share the relevant property.
- Put the narrowest conditioned forms before a less restricted or elsewhere form.
- Do not duplicate the same unrestricted form for every stem. Do not use an environment broader than the evidence, such as “after any consonant” when only one class is supported.
- Check whether the forms are truly one morpheme before treating their difference as phonological conditioning.

Existing ordinary alternate text can be edited in place with [Edit an allomorph form](cmd:compose-edit-allomorph-form) (`motif_edit_allomorph_form`), naming its expected owner, writing system and current text. This keeps conditions and references on the same form ID. Lexeme forms use [Rewrite lexeme forms](cmd:compose-rewrite-lexeme-form) with explicit `newForm` and `foldStressMarks=false` when underlying distinctions condition the grammar. [Edit a citation form](cmd:compose-edit-citation-form) (`motif_edit_citation_form`) retains a selected marked source headword separately from parser forms.

## Motif support

`motif_lexicon` with detailed results can read existing allomorphs and their environments. `motif_grammar` can read natural classes and environments. `motif_add_phoneme`, `motif_add_natural_class` and `motif_add_environment` create the sound inventory and context. `motif_add_lexeme_form` changes an existing lexeme form. `motif_add_alternate_form` creates a stem or affix alternate under an existing entry. It accepts optional sound `environments` and, for affix forms, optional `inflectionClasses`. When alternates already exist, supply an exact `placement` gap. `motif_add_affix_process_allomorph` adds a pattern-based form (an affix process with its own input and output) to an affix entry whose other forms may be plain allomorphs or processes; it takes no environments and applies to all of the entry's grammatical info. `motif_add_alternate_form` likewise adds a plain affix allomorph beside process forms. Both take `inflectionClasses` for inflectional grammatical info; the parser ignores them for a derivational analysis (the stem features an allomorph requires, `MsEnvFeatures` in LibLCM, are read for a derivational affix too, but Motif has no composer for them yet), so a mixed entry can use them for its inflectional analysis while restricting the derivational analysis through the `motif_edit_derivational_affix_restriction` MCP tool or `compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction` CLI verb (guide suffix-prefix-slots). When the entry has no inflectional grammatical info, Motif refuses `inflectionClasses` and points to that composer. `motif_edit_allomorph_condition`, when selected by the profile, can link an environment to an existing allomorph.

## What an allomorph can and cannot carry

FieldWorks holds the meaning of a morpheme on the entry, not on its forms. So one form cannot have its own tense, gloss or slot.

| An allomorph can carry | An allomorph cannot carry |
|---|---|
| Sound environments the form occurs in (`environments`) | Its own gloss, tense or other label |
| Inflection classes of the stems it attaches to, for an inflectional analysis (`inflectionClasses`) | Its own grammatical info or slot |
| For an affix, the stem features and category it needs (conditions on the stem it attaches to) | A different category or meaning from the entry's other forms |
| For a stem, a stem name tied to inflection features | A rule to apply or skip (use exception features on the analysis) |
| Its place in the order of the entry's forms | Anything that changes which senses it serves |
| Being abstract (a form no word shows) | |

When the form needs a different label, as a past form beside a future one, make it its own entry with its own grammatical info, slot and sense. Two analyses on one entry do not help: the parser gives every form of the entry to every analysis, so both labels would apply to both forms.

## Two forms that must not block each other (free variation)

An earlier form with an environment blocks every later form of the same entry wherever it matches, the lexeme form (always last) included. HermitCrab's one exception is free fluctuation: neighbouring forms whose environment sets are exactly equal are not disjunctive, so both parse and neither blocks the other. For an affix this is the only encoding; an affix variant entry is not read by the parser. A stem can also be a variant entry with no sense of its own, which the parser loads as a separate stem, but that is a different morpheme, not a form of this one.

- To let the plain suffix `an` and a variant that starts with a hyphen character, `-an`, both parse after any sound, give the entry two forms with no environment. `motif_add_alternate_form` with no `environments` does this; leave the new form last, beside the unrestricted lexeme form. A real-parser test (`AuthorFreeVariationParserTests`) shows two spellings (`an` and `ang`) both parse after `o` and after `a`.
- Two alternates that carry the same environments are free variation with each other (the same test file shows both parse where the environment matches, and the plain lexeme form is blocked there). A form whose environments differ from its neighbour's is not free variation. An alternate restricted to "after a consonant" blocks the lexeme form after every consonant, so the plain spelling stops parsing there. The parser has no way to say "this form where the environment matches, and the plain form everywhere as well".
- Best workaround when the variant should occur only in one context but the plain form must stay possible there too: make the variant unrestricted (free variation) and accept that it also licenses the variant in other contexts, such as a hyphen after a vowel; measure that over-generation with a Trial.

## A hyphenated spelling of an affix process

An affix process cannot carry a written alternate form: it has no spelling of its own, only an input and an output. When the text writes a hyphen between the affix and the stem (Cebuano `l`-forms and `X-X` reduplication), make the hyphen part of the output. Add a second process to the same entry with `compose-author-affix-process-allomorph` (`motif_add_affix_process_allomorph`) whose output inserts the hyphen phoneme where the text writes it, for example `{"insert":["<i>","<k>","<a>","<hyphen>"]},{"copy":"rest"}` beside the process that inserts the same sounds without the hyphen. The hyphen must be a phoneme (`compose-author-phoneme`). LibLCM holds the entry's processes as ordered alternate forms of one entry, so both spellings share its gloss and grammatical info and the real parser reads either; for full reduplication a single process that copies the stem, inserts the hyphen and copies it again already gives the hyphenated spelling, so no second process is needed. A plain written alternate (`compose-author-alternate-form`) may share the entry with processes when it expresses a written realization rather than a pattern change.

Do not add a shape-restricted solid form to the entry of an unrestricted hyphen form. A form earlier in the order blocks every later form of the entry for the stems it matches, so a solid form restricted to, say, three-sound stems stops the hyphen spelling of exactly those stems (`RealParserReduplicationBlockingTests` shows `pul-pul` lost while `kaun-kaun` still parses). That is the loss an earlier round saw when it put shape forms on the hyphen entry. Give the restricted solid form its own entry: both spellings then parse, each by its own entry.

## Replace a process with a plain archiphoneme form

Keep the entry, its senses and grammatical analyses. In one Draft, author a plain alternate with `compose-author-alternate-form`, then move each prohibition occurrence to that form with [Retarget a prohibition](cmd:compose-edit-adhoc-prohibition-references). Use [Delete a prohibition](cmd:compose-delete-adhoc-prohibition) for restrictions that should disappear. Supply the complete expected state, including Disabled and legacy allomorph references. Morpheme prohibitions can keep their grammatical-analysis references when the entry and analyses stay the same.

Finally use [Delete an affix process](cmd:compose-delete-affix-process) with `entry`, the process `form` and the plain form as `replacement`. A lexeme process is replaced by promoting the plain alternate; an alternate process is removed while the plain form stays. The command refuses until every reference into the process graph has moved or gone, naming each remaining occurrence and its remedy. These steps can be one `compose` request, with an earlier step's created form referenced by its label. MCP stages only; a person reviews the Dry Run and Trial and Applies.
